item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q005_cupredoxin_function_transfer","answer":"SCOPe 2.08 places all three in the all-beta class (b), Cupredoxin-like fold (b.6), and Cupredoxins superfamily (b.6.1), implying probable remote homology/common ancestry. They are nevertheless separate families: Plastocyanin/azurin-like (b.6.1.1; SUNID 49504), Ephrin ectodomain (b.6.1.5; SUNID 74874), and the PAD4 N-terminal domain (b.6.1.6; SUNID 110107). Thus they are not family-level equivalents. SCOPe explicitly describes the ephrin and PAD4 families as probably related to cupredoxins but lacking the metal-binding site. Copper binding or electron-transfer activity therefore must not be transferred from plastocyanin/azurin to ephrin ectodomains or PAD4's N-terminal domain; superfamily membership establishes neither activity. A cross-family b.6.1 template may support the overall beta-sandwich/core fold, but not copper-site geometry, ligand placement, or redox function. Such functions require target-specific evidence—for example conservation and compatible three-dimensional arrangement of copper-ligating residues, direct metal-binding/spectroscopic measurements, and electron-transfer or redox assays. Even a b.6.1.1 label alone should not replace protein-specific functional evidence.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info: /api/v1/releases/current","mcp__scope__search_scop: /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=plastocyanin+azurin&mode=auto&limit=50; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=ephrin&mode=auto&limit=50; /api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=peptidylarginine&mode=auto&limit=50","mcp__scope__get_scop_node: /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49503; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49503/parents; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49503/homology; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/49504; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/74874; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/74874/annotations; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/110107; /api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/110107/annotations"]}]}
